acceptance: Python SDK passes compatibility tests against current and previous supported daemon.
verifiedBy: python3 tests/sdk/python_package_boundary_test.py && python3 tests/sdk/python_daemon_compatibility_test.py && python3 -m unittest tests.sdk.python_client_test tests.sdk.python_package_boundary_test tests.sdk.python_daemon_compatibility_test && node --test tests/sdk/http-transport-contract.test.mjs tests/sdk/cross-language-compat.test.mjs; final confirmation deferred to the Book 3 Wave 4 gate's node scripts/release/verify-release-plan.mjs --task MBR-909 and pnpm test against the integrated tree.

demonstration.currentAndPreviousDaemon: schemas/context-receipt.v1.schema.json types ContextReceiptV1.schemaVersion as the enum [1, 2]: 2 is what a current daemon emits ('the planner always populates the v2 observability fields'), 1 is what a previous supported daemon emitted and the client must still accept. tests/sdk/python_daemon_compatibility_test.py reads that enum directly from the schema at test time (not a hard-coded copy), then: (1) asserts membrane_client.analyze_receipt() accepts every version currently in that enum without raising and reports the correct schema_version back; (2) asserts the oldest supported version (the 'previous supported daemon') is still non-degraded on its own merits, not merely tolerated; (3) asserts a version one past the newest in the enum (a hypothetical future, not-yet-supported daemon) is rejected with ProtocolError(code='protocol_version_unsupported'); (4) asserts the schema still advertises at least two supported versions, so if a future daemon change drops back to one version this test's premise fails loudly instead of the loop silently covering only one case.
demonstration.packagingDoesNotPublishTheCoreApp: packages/python/package-boundary.v1.json (validated against schemas/sdk-python-package-boundary.v1.schema.json) declares allowedTopLevelPackages=['membrane_client'], runtimeDependencies=[], forbiddenPathPrefixes covering the Rust engine/daemon (engine/), the desktop app (apps/), installer/release tooling (packaging/, release/, install/, npm/), and the other language SDK (packages/typescript/), forbiddenFileExtensions covering native binaries/installers/archives, and corePublishing={publishesCoreApp:false, bundlesDaemonBinary:false} typed as schema const:false. tests/sdk/python_package_boundary_test.py's PackageBoundaryMatchesRealPackageTest cross-checks every one of those claims against the real pyproject.toml (packages.find where, zero project.dependencies, no forbidden-prefix substring anywhere in the file's own text) and the real on-disk package tree (reimplementing setuptools' find: discovery rule directly, since setuptools is not installed in this environment and this task adds no new dependency; no forbidden extension present anywhere under packages/python/).
demonstration.typedClientClaimIsMechanical: src/membrane_client/py.typed (PEP 561) plus pyproject.toml's [tool.setuptools.package-data] membrane_client=['py.typed'] and tests/sdk/python_package_boundary_test.py's test_py_typed_marker_is_shipped_and_declared make this package's 'typed client' description true for downstream type checkers rather than only prose.
demonstration.noUnattendedPublish: No PyPI/index publish command, credential, or automation was added by this task. docs/sdk/python-publishing.md states explicitly that publishing stays a separately authorized release action and that this source change does not publish, does not run a build, and adds no automation that could publish unattended -- mirroring docs/sdk/publishing.md's identical statement for the Rust crates (MBR-908).
